summary: Xiaoting Wei specializes in Sinology and Buddhist studies. She earned an MA at the National University of Singapore under Kathy Ku Cheng Mei (attested 2004).

Xinchuan Huang (1928–2021) was a scholar of philosophy, Indology, and Buddhist studies. He studied at Peking University (~1948–1952) and held a research post at the Chinese Academy of Social Sciences (~1978).

Xinru Liu works in Indology, history, archaeology, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. She completed her PhD under Ludo Rocher at the University of Pennsylvania (~1980–1985), later holding professorships at CASS (1993) and The College of New Jersey (~1999).
Xiuzhi Zeng specializes in Buddhist and religious studies. She earned an MA at Nanhua University under the supervision of Meihua Chen (attested 2006).

Xu Dishan (1893–1941) was a Sinology, Buddhist, and religious studies scholar. Educated at Yenching, Columbia, and Oxford, he held posts at Peking University (~1927–1935), Tsinghua University (~1928–1930), and the University of Hong Kong (~1935–1941).

Xuesong Zhang is a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies who earned a PhD at The Chinese University of Hong Kong under Xueyu (attested 2008). He served as associate professor at Renmin University of China (attested 2015).

Xuezhu Li specializes in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and Indology, having studied under Shoryu Katsura. He served as a Research Associate at China Tibetology Research Center (attested 2010–2022) and a Numata fellow at Ryukoku University (2011).

Y. Karunadasa (1934–2026) studied Buddhist studies and philosophy at University of Ceylon and SOAS under David Friedman. He served as professor at University of Kelaniya (~1969–2000) and Director of the Postgraduate Institute of Pali and Buddhist Studies (~1993–2000, 2008).

Yael Bentor specializes in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. She studied at the Hebrew University of Jerusalem and Indiana University under Gregory Schopen and others, and taught in the Department of Indian Studies at the Hebrew University of Jerusalem (attested 1995–2000).

Yamada Koun (1907–1989) was a Buddhist studies and religious studies master who studied at the University of Tokyo (~1927–1930) and under several Zen teachers. In 1970, he became the second head of Sanbo Zen.
Yanfei Zhou specializes in Buddhist studies, history, archaeology, and Sinology. She completed her PhD at the National University of Singapore under the supervision of Yuet-Keung Lo.

Yang Renshan (1837–1911) was a scholar in Buddhist studies and Sinology. He founded the Jinling Scriptural Press (1897), the Jetavana Hermitage (1908), and the Buddhist Research Society (1910), which he headed in 1910.
Yang-Gyu An specializes in Buddhist studies. He earned a D.Phil. from the University of Oxford by 1998 under the supervision of Richard Gombrich, and also studied under Hojin (attested 2003).
Yangdon Dhondup (b. 1970) is a Tibetology scholar. She completed her PhD at SOAS University of London (~2000–2004) under the supervision of Henry Y. H. Zhao.
Yanling Chen specializes in Buddhist studies. She completed an MA at Fo Guang University under Yongdong Shi and studied under Hsing Yun (attested 2012).
Yanpei (1917–1996) was a scholar of Buddhist studies. He studied under Taixu (~1934–1947) and Yin Shun (~1941).
Yao Wang (1928–2015) was a scholar of Tibetology and Sinology who studied under Gongkar Tulku. He held a post as a guest professor at the University of Vienna.
Yao-ming Tsai specializes in Buddhist studies and philosophy. He earned his PhD at the University of California by 1997 and served as Professor of Philosophy at National Taiwan University.
Yaping Dou specializes in religious and Buddhist studies. She earned her PhD at The Chinese University of Hong Kong under the supervision of Xueyu (attested 2010).

Yaroslav Komarovski specializes in Tibetology and Buddhist studies, having trained at several monastic institutes and the University of Virginia. He held a fellowship at Washington University in St. Louis and a post at the University of Nebraska–Lincoln (attested 2011).
